claim: For every integer n with 5 <= n <= 15 and every nonnegative real n x n matrix A whose entries sum to n, phi(A) := prod_i r_i(A) + prod_j c_j(A) - per(A) <= 2 - n!/n^n, with equality if and only if A = J_n/n.

quadruple.statement: For every integer n with 5 <= n <= 15 and every nonnegative real n x n matrix A whose entries sum to n, phi(A) := prod_i r_i(A) + prod_j c_j(A) - per(A) <= 2 - n!/n^n, with equality if and only if A = J_n/n.
quadruple.stage: real polynomial inequality on the compact simplex K_n in R^{n x n}, one finite-dimensional statement for each of the eleven values n = 5..15

shape.objects: A ranges over K_n, a compact simplex of dimension n^2 - 1 (finite-dimensional); n ranges over the finite set {5,...,15}; phi is a polynomial of degree n in the n^2 entries; r_i, c_j are linear, per(A) is the permanent.
shape.quantifiers: universal over A in K_n for each of eleven fixed n; the equality clause is uniqueness: for all A in K_n, phi(A) = 2 - n!/n^n implies A = J_n/n.
shape.target_quantity: a sharp explicit constant per n: max of phi on K_n equals 2 - n!/n^n, attained only at J_n/n; the quantitative form (the n=4 paper, and the fallback named in the input) asks for an explicit rational c_1(n) > 0 with 2 - n!/n^n - phi(A) >= c_1 ||A - J_n/n||_F^2 on K_n.
shape.ambient_structure: polynomial optimisation on a simplex (order: x_ij >= 0; algebra: degree-n polynomial phi; one linear equality sum x_ij = n); inside K_n sits the doubly stochastic polytope Omega_n, where phi = 2 - per and the claim is the van der Waerden theorem; Sinkhorn scaling connects fully indecomposable A to Omega_n; the Hall-type criterion s(S[I,J]) >= |I|+|J|-n characterises doubly superstochastic S. The simpler ambient that keeps the constraint is Omega_n.
shape.symmetries: phi and K_n are invariant under G_n = (S_n x S_n) semidirect Z_2 (row permutations, column permutations, transpose), of order 2 (n!)^2; J_n/n is the unique G_n-fixed point of K_n; phi is not invariant under Sinkhorn scaling (row/column sums change).
shape.configuration: no forbidden configuration; the difficulty is the boundary of K_n: a maximiser with a zero entry (Hwang 1986: every positive maximiser is J_n/n; Cheon-Wanless 2012 Thm 3.2 and 3.7: a maximiser is fully indecomposable and its zeros do not form a single block). The algebraic relation is the linear equality sum x_ij = n; all other constraints are the inequalities x_ij >= 0.
shape.extremal_candidate: known: J_n/n, unique up to symmetry (it is G_n-fixed); phi has a strict local maximum there (Hwang 1986); phi(J_n/n) = 2 - n!/n^n.
shape.finite_certificates: the true side has a finite certificate at each fixed n: an exact rational constrained sum-of-squares identity for the gap polynomial on the simplex (n=4, arXiv:2607.29191), or a rational inequality that closes the boundary-exclusion argument (n=16, arXiv:2607.19439, where the whole proof is dimension-generic except one rational comparison). The false side also has a finite certificate: an explicit A in K_n with phi(A) > 2 - n!/n^n, checkable in exact arithmetic.
shape.monotonicity: not monotone in n in any proved sense: n = 2, 3, 4 and n >= 16 are proved by three different methods. The boundary-exclusion inequality of arXiv:2607.19439 holds iff n >= 16 (exact over Q, study/kafidov-threshold.py: ratio 1.869 at 16, 0.987 at 15, 0.535 at 14, 0.298 at 13, 0.172 at 12, 0.104 at 11). Smallest open parameter n = 5; largest n = 15.
shape.uniformity_parameter: n. Each n is a separate finite-dimensional statement. On the analytic route the difficulty is the relative gap (m_n - gamma_n)/gamma_n ~ 1/(2 (n-1)^2) between the Knopp-Sinkhorn boundary minimum m_n and gamma_n = n!/n^n, against the dilation loss ~ n^3 m_n^2, which shrinks faster; that route works for large n. On the computational route the difficulty is the certificate degree 2*ceil(n/2) and the Gram basis size C(n^2 + ceil(n/2) - 1, ceil(n/2)); that route works for small n.
shape.proof_shape: two shapes in print. (i) Boundary exclusion (Cheon-Wanless 2012, Pang 2606.01531, Kafidov 2607.19439): a maximiser with a zero has per(A) = gamma_n - delta, 0 < delta <= gamma_n; row-product deficit rho and column-product deficit sigma satisfy rho + sigma <= delta; AM-GM plus Pinsker give every subset row sum within sqrt(n rho/2) of its size; the Hall criterion then makes (1-t)^{-1} A doubly superstochastic with t = sqrt(n delta/(1-delta)); Knopp-Sinkhorn gives per >= m_n on the boundary of Omega_n; the contradiction m_n (1-t)^n > gamma_n - delta for all delta needs m_n - gamma_n > n^3 m_n^2/(4(1-gamma_n)), which loses the factor n^3 m_n^2 (the uniform dilation of all n rows against an l2 deviation of order sqrt(delta)) and stops at n = 16. Hwang's positive-support theorem finishes. (ii) Exact SOS certificate (Li-Xiong-Yang 2607.29191, n = 4): gap polynomial Q_n - lambda ||A - U_n||_F^2 in the truncated pairwise preordering sigma_0 + sum x_i sigma_i + sum x_i x_j sigma_ij + h q at the minimal degree; numerical SDP (MOSEK); centering out the null vector at U_n; sequential rational recovery with a common denominator; exact LDL^T over Q; coefficient comparison; Lean 4 check by native_decide. What (ii) loses per step: the degree bound may be insufficient at higher n (unknown for n >= 5), and rational recovery must handle the singular equality point.
shape.neighbours: van der Waerden conjecture (phi on Omega_n): known true (Egorychev, Falikman 1981). Knopp-Sinkhorn minimum of per on Omega_n with a zero, n > 3: known, m_n = (n-2)!((n-2)/(n-1)^2)^{n-2} (1982). Dittert n = 2 (Sinkhorn 1984), n = 3 (Hwang 1987), n = 4 (2607.29191), n = 16 (2607.19439), n >= 17 (2606.01531): known true. Dittert for row-stochastic A: known true (Hwang). Partly decomposable A is not a maximiser: known (CW Thm 3.2). Single-block zero pattern is not a maximiser: known (CW Thm 3.7). Every maximiser on K_4 is fully indecomposable: known (Udayan-Somasundaram 2024). Quantitative stability with explicit c_1: known at n = 4 (c_1 = 1/52), open for 5..15. Lih-Wang convexity conjecture for per on Omega_n: open. Dittert for 5 <= n <= 15: open (this claim).
shape.known_bounds: Upper side (how far a counterexample could be from the conjecture): Cheon-Wanless Thm 2.1: for phi(A) >= phi(J_n), 0 <= delta <= n!/n^n and every k-subset row or column sum is within sqrt(2 delta k) of k; Thm 2.4: per(A) > (1 - sqrt(8 delta n^3 gamma_n)) gamma_n, so delta = O(n^4 e^{-2n}); Hwang: row and column sums of a maximiser lie in [1 - sqrt(2 gamma_n), 1 + (n-1) sqrt(2 gamma_n)]. Method: AM-GM and the Hall criterion. Lower side: phi(J_n/n) = 2 - gamma_n is attained. Documented ceilings: the boundary-exclusion inequality m_n - gamma_n > n^3 m_n^2/(4(1-gamma_n)) holds iff n >= 16 (exact over Q), and its Bernoulli-free form fails at n = 15 by 2.1e-5 gamma_15 against a gap of 2.5e-3 gamma_15 and at n = 14 by 2.5e-3 gamma_14 against 2.9e-3 gamma_14 (60-digit evidence, study/kafidov-threshold.py). The SOS route's documented scale: n = 4 needed a 153-monomial main block and 136 blocks of 17; at n = 5 the unreduced main Gram has 2925 monomials.
shape.missing_input: On the analytic route: a lower bound on per(A) for a near-doubly-stochastic A in K_n with a zero entry (equivalently on the capacity cap(A) = inf_x prod_i (Ax)_i / prod_j x_j, since per(A) >= cap(A) m_n by Sinkhorn scaling and Knopp-Sinkhorn) that loses less than the uniform-dilation factor (1-t)^n ~ 1 - n^{1.5} sqrt(delta). On the computational route: whether a certificate exists at degree 2*ceil(n/2) in the symmetry-reduced pairwise preordering, unknown for every n >= 5.
shape.base_theory: ZFC. For each n the claim is a sentence of the first-order theory of real closed fields (a polynomial inequality on a compact basic semialgebraic set), decidable in principle. No hypothesis beyond ZFC bears on it or on any neighbour. The machine checks (exact rational LDL^T, exact rational comparison, coefficient comparison over Q) stay inside Lean's standard axioms (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound) when done by kernel reduction, and add Lean.ofReduceBool (the compiler in the trusted base) when done by native_decide, as the n = 4 Lean check does (arXiv:2607.29191, main.tex lines 973-993).

known: Every positive maximiser of phi on K_n is J_n/n; phi has a strict local maximum at J_n/n; row and column sums of a maximiser lie in [1 - sqrt(2 n!/n^n), 1 + (n-1) sqrt(2 n!/n^n)]: Hwang, Linear Algebra Appl. 76 (1986) 31-44, doi:10.1016/0024-3795(86)90212-0.

For phi(A) >= phi(J_n): 0 <= delta := gamma_n - per(A) <= gamma_n, every k-subset row or column sum within sqrt(2 delta k) of k (Thm 2.1); per(A) > (1 - sqrt(8 delta n^3 gamma_n)) gamma_n (Thm 2.4); a partly decomposable A is not a maximiser (Thm 3.2); zeros forming a single block cannot occur in a maximiser (Thm 3.7); Li's criterion for doubly superstochastic matrices (Lemma 2.2): Cheon and Wanless, Linear Algebra Appl. 436 (2012) 791-801, doi:10.1016/j.laa.2010.08.041.

Minimum permanent on doubly stochastic matrices with a zero entry, n > 3, equals m_n = (n-2)! ((n-2)/(n-1)^2)^(n-2): Knopp and Sinkhorn, Linear Multilinear Algebra 11 (1982) 351-355, doi:10.1080/03081088208817459.
per(B) >= n!/n^n on Omega_n with equality only at J_n/n: Egorychev (1981), Falikman (1981).
Every phi-maximising matrix on K_4 is fully indecomposable: Udayan and Somasundaram, Special Matrices 12 (2024) 20240006, arXiv:2312.00464.
n >= 17: Pang, arXiv:2606.01531 (2026-06-01), boundary exclusion with dilation t = sqrt(3 n delta); the numeric condition m_n - gamma_n > (3/4) n^3 m_n^2 holds iff n >= 17.

n = 16: Kafidov, arXiv:2607.19439 (2026-07-21), joint-deficit dilation t = sqrt(n delta/(1-delta)); the numeric condition m_n - gamma_n > n^3 m_n^2/(4(1-gamma_n)) holds iff n >= 16 (exact over Q for 4 <= n <= 17: study/kafidov-threshold.py, 2026-09-03).

n = 4, with 61/32 - phi(A) >= (1/52) ||A - U_4||_F^2: Li, Xiong and Yang, arXiv:2607.29191v2 (2026-07-31), exact rational constrained SOS certificate (main block 153, 136 blocks of 17, denominator 1331), Lean 4 check with native_decide.
Conjecture 28 in Minc, Linear Multilinear Algebra 12 (1983) 227-263; Conjecture 14 in Zhan, Open problems in matrix theory, ICCM 2007.
